question: How do I replace a worn-out shut-off valve under my kitchen sink?
answer: To replace a worn-out shut-off valve, first shut off the water supply to the valve by locating the main shut-off valve and turning it clockwise. Then, disconnect the water supply lines from the valve and remove the valve from the pipe. Next, apply penetrating oil to the old valve's threads and let it sit for a few minutes to loosen any corrosion. Use a valve removal tool to remove the old valve, taking care not to damage the pipe. Install the new valve, ensuring it is properly seated and secured. Finally, reconnect the water supply lines and turn on the water supply to test the new valve.
steps: Shut off the water supply to the valve
Disconnect the water supply lines from the valve
Remove the valve from the pipe
Apply penetrating oil to the old valve's threads
Use a valve removal tool to remove the old valve
safety_info: When working with plumbing, be aware of the risk of water shock, which can occur when the water supply is turned back on and can cause injury or damage. To mitigate this risk, turn on the water supply slowly and check for leaks.
